title: Thinning and sprinkling: from robust sampling to almost Hamiltonicity
summary: We develop the thinning--sprinkling technique, a general method for proving robustness of graph properties under random vertex sampling. Using it, we show that random induced subgraphs of tough graphs, high-degree connected vertex-transitive graphs, and nearly regular sublinear expanders retain strong connectivity or expansion properties with very high probability. We also prove that every $k$-connected graph with $k=ω(\log n)$ contains a spanning bipartite subgraph that is $Ω(k)$-connected.
